message.content: Lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) are both placental mammals, but they belong to different orders—Carnivora for lions and Perissodactyla for zebras. Their most recent common ancestor is therefore the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**, which contains the orders Carnivora, Perissodactyla, Artiodactyla, Chiroptera, and Cetartiodactyla. This ancestor would have been a small, early mammal that lived roughly 60–70 million years ago, before the lineages that led to modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates split apart.
